dataset.what_one_row_represents: One scheduled 2026 FIFA World Cup match (date, match number, group, stadium), joinable to per-venue historical climate via venue_weather.csv on the stadium key.

ana_01.label: Clean 104-match schedule, perfect weather join
ana_01.content: The schedule contains 104 matches over 34 distinct match days (11 June to 19 July 2026), played at exactly 16 unique stadiums. The venue_weather.csv file carries one row per venue and joins to the schedule on the stadium column with zero unmatched rows: all 16 schedule stadiums have a climate record. This makes the location-and-weather join clean and complete, with no missing venues to caveat.

calculation.output:
schedule rows=104 fixtures rows=104 weather rows=16
unique stadiums in schedule=16
unique stadiums in weather=16
date range 2026-06-11 -> 2026-07-19 across 34 match days
stadiums in schedule with NO weather match: none

ana_02.label: Matches per venue: Dallas leads with 9
ana_02.content: Match load is uneven across the 16 venues. Dallas (AT&T Stadium, Arlington) hosts the most with 9 matches, followed by Los Angeles (SoFi), New York/New Jersey (MetLife) and Atlanta (Mercedes-Benz) at 8 each. A middle tier of Boston, Vancouver, Houston and Miami host 7, while Mexico's venues sit at the bottom: Mexico City 5, Guadalajara and Monterrey 4 each. The busiest venues are concentrated in the hot southern U.S. and the populous Northeast.

calculation.output:
9  Dallas Stadium ... Arlington
 8  Los Angeles Stadium ... Inglewood
 8  New York New Jersey Stadium ... East Rutherford
 8  Atlanta Stadium ... Atlanta
 7  Boston / BC Place Vancouver / Houston / Miami
 6  Toronto / SF Bay / Philadelphia / Seattle / Kansas City
 5  Mexico City
 4  Guadalajara / Monterrey
total matches = 104

ana_03.label: USA hosts 78 of 104 matches
ana_03.content: The host load is heavily skewed to the United States, which stages 78 of the 104 matches across its 11 venues, while Canada (2 venues) and Mexico (3 venues) host 13 each. This matches FIFA's announced split and means three-quarters of the tournament is played in the country with the broadest internal climate range — from cool Seattle to scorching Houston.

calculation.output:
USA: 78 matches across 11 venues
Mexico: 13 matches across 3 venues
Canada: 13 matches across 2 venues

data_table.description: Matches and venues per host nation

ana_04.label: Feels-like spread of 17.1C across venues
ana_04.content: Ranking all 16 venues by average apparent (feels-like) high temperature in the tournament window reveals an enormous spread. Houston tops it at 38.6C feels-like, with Dallas/Arlington at 38.3C, Miami at 36.9C and Monterrey at 36.2C. At the cool end sit Vancouver (21.5C), Seattle (23.1C) and Mexico City (24.3C, tempered by its altitude). The gap between the hottest and coolest venue is 17.1C — the difference between dangerous heat-stress conditions and a mild spring afternoon, within the same tournament.

calculation.output:
38.6C feels (33.5C air) hum 76.5% Houston / NRG Stadium
 38.3C feels (34.9C air) hum 61.6% Arlington / AT&T Stadium
 36.9C feels (31.0C air) hum 82.9% Miami Gardens
 36.2C feels Monterrey
 ...
 23.1C Seattle
 21.5C Vancouver
feels-like spread: 38.6C (Houston) to 21.5C (Vancouver) = 17.1C

data_table.description: Feels-like (apparent) high vs air high vs humidity, all 16 venues, hottest first

ana_05.label: A third of all matches in dangerous heat
ana_05.content: Combining match load with climate shows where the most football is played in the most heat. Weighting each venue's matches by its feels-like high, Dallas tops the 'heat exposure' index (9 matches x 38.3C), followed by Atlanta, Houston and Miami. Crucially, 35 of the 104 matches (33.7%) are at venues whose typical feels-like high is 34C or more, and 41 matches (39.4%) fall at the six venues FIFPRO flagged as 'extremely high risk' for heat-stress injury. So roughly four in ten World Cup matches are scheduled into the climate band that prompted the player-welfare alarm.

calculation.output:
344.7  Arlington   9 matches x 38.3C
  272.8  Atlanta     8 x 34.1C
  270.2  Houston     7 x 38.6C
  258.3  Miami Gardens 7 x 36.9C
 ...
matches at venues with feels-like >= 34C: 35 of 104 = 33.7%
matches at FIFPRO 'extremely high risk' 6 venues: 41 of 104 = 39.4%

data_table.description: Heat-exposure index = matches x feels-like high, descending

ana_06.label: Rain: Miami soaks 88% of days, LA almost never
ana_06.content: Precipitation exposure is just as polarized as heat. Miami sees rain on 88% of days in the tournament window (8.4 mm/day), with Mexico's altitude cities close behind (Guadalajara 73%, Mexico City 72%) reflecting the North American summer monsoon and afternoon thunderstorms. At the opposite extreme, Santa Clara records rain on 0% of sampled days and Inglewood (LA) just 1% — California's bone-dry summer. Seattle, despite its rainy reputation, is dry in midsummer at 13%. Wet venues raise the risk of weather delays and lightning stoppages; dry-but-hot venues trade that for heat stress.

calculation.output:
88% wet days  8.4mm/day Miami Gardens
   73% Guadalajara
   72% Mexico City
 ...
    1% Inglewood
    0% Santa Clara

data_table.description: Rainy-day share (% of days with rain) and mean precip, all 16 venues

ana_07.label: Altitude: Mexico City at 2,200 m towers over the field
ana_07.content: Elevation varies by more than two kilometres across venues. Mexico City's Estadio Azteca sits at 2,200 m, far above any other venue and high enough to measurably reduce aerobic capacity and ball aerodynamics; Guadalajara follows at 1,566 m and Monterrey at 450 m. Every other venue is below 330 m, and the final venue MetLife sits essentially at sea level (2 m). Altitude is the reason Mexico City stays mild despite its low latitude: thin mountain air keeps its feels-like high to just 24.3C even as it sits at the same latitude as the Sahara.

calculation.output:
2200m  Mexico City (Estadio Azteca)
 1566m  Guadalajara
  450m  Monterrey
  ...
    2m  East Rutherford (MetLife Stadium)

data_table.description: Venue elevation in metres, highest first

ana_08.label: Four climate tribes: brutal, dry-hot, warm, mild
ana_08.content: Plotting feels-like high against humidity sorts the 16 venues into four tribes. Three are 'brutal' — hot AND humid: Houston (38.6C, 76%), Miami (36.9C, 83%) and Atlanta (34.1C, 73%). Two are 'dry-hot' — fierce air temperature but lower humidity, where evaporative cooling and roofs help: Dallas (38.3C, 62%) and Monterrey (36.2C, 64%). Six are 'warm', and five are genuinely 'mild' (feels-like at or below 27C): Mexico City, Toronto, Vancouver, Seattle and Santa Clara. The brutal tribe is the player-welfare hotspot; the mild tribe is where European players will feel most at home.

calculation.output:
Houston feels 38.6C hum 76.5% -> brutal (hot+humid)
Miami feels 36.9C hum 82.9% -> brutal
Atlanta feels 34.1C hum 72.8% -> brutal
Arlington 38.3C hum 61.6% -> dry-hot
Monterrey 36.2C hum 63.6% -> dry-hot
...
buckets: {'mild': 5, 'warm': 6, 'dry-hot': 2, 'brutal (hot+humid)': 3}

data_table.description: Feels-like vs humidity scatter with bubble=matches and climate tribe

ana_09.label: Geo-climate master table for the interactive map
ana_09.content: The full per-venue table for the interactive map combines coordinates, elevation, climate and match load for all 16 stadiums. Fifteen venues have a real licensed stadium photo; Kansas City (Arrowhead Stadium) has no cached photo and must be handled with a placeholder rather than a fake image. The continental footprint runs from Vancouver (49.3N, the coolest) down to Mexico City (19.3N, the highest) and Miami (the wettest), spanning four time zones.

ana_10.label: 39-day calendar peaks at 6 matches a day
ana_10.content: The tournament unfolds over 39 days and 34 match days. It opens softly on 11 June with 2 matches, ramps through a dense group stage that peaks at 6 matches in a single day (24 June), then thins to one match per day in the late knockout rounds, ending with the final on 19 July. The dense group-stage days are when the most venues run simultaneously, multiplying the number of pitches exposed to peak afternoon heat on any given day.

calculation.output:
first day 2026-06-11 (2 matches), last 2026-07-19 (1)
busiest day: 2026-06-24 with 6 matches

data_table.description: Matches per match-day (sampled key days; full 34-day series in code)

ana_11.label: Humidity drives the feels-like penalty
ana_11.content: Why does Houston (33.5C air) feel hotter than Dallas (34.9C air)? Humidity. The gap between feels-like and air temperature is largest at the most humid venues: Miami adds +5.9C, Houston +5.1C, while dry Santa Clara actually feels 0.6C cooler than its air temperature. Across all 16 venues the correlation between humidity and the feels-like penalty is positive (Pearson r = 0.49). This is the meteorological mechanism behind the player-welfare concern: it is not just heat, it is heat the body cannot shed by sweating.

calculation.output:
+5.9C feels-gap hum 82.9% Miami Gardens
 +5.1C feels-gap hum 76.5% Houston
 ...
 -0.6C feels-gap hum 62.3% Santa Clara
pearson(humidity, feels-gap) = 0.49

data_table.description: Feels-like minus air-high gap vs humidity, all venues

ana_12.label: The headline extremes
ana_12.content: The dataset's extremes frame the whole story: hottest feels-like venue is Houston at 38.6C; coolest is Vancouver at 21.5C; wettest is Miami with rain on 88% of days; driest is Santa Clara at 0%; highest is Mexico City at 2,200 m; and the single hottest day recorded in the window at any venue was Monterrey at 42.5C. These six numbers are the stat callouts that anchor the location-and-weather narrative.

calculation.output:
hottest feels-like: Houston 38.6C
coolest feels-like: Vancouver 21.5C
wettest: Miami Gardens 88% of days
driest: Santa Clara 0% of days
highest altitude: Mexico City 2200m
hottest single day on record in window: Monterrey 42.5C

caveats.content: All weather figures are TYPICAL historical climate for the 11 Jun-19 Jul window averaged over 2021-2024 (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0), NOT a 2026 forecast for any specific match date. They describe the loaded dice, not the roll.

Apparent (feels-like) temperature approximates a heat index from air temperature, humidity, wind and radiation; it is not the WBGT metric FIFA/FIFPRO use for thresholds, though it tracks the same heat-stress concept.

Raw climate ignores stadium roofs and air conditioning. Dallas (AT&T), Houston (NRG) and Atlanta (Mercedes-Benz) have full climate control that buffers their high feels-like numbers; BC Place's roof will be OPEN for 2026 and MetLife has no roof. Heat numbers are the hazard, not the experienced condition.
Fixtures include playoff placeholder team names (e.g. slash-separated opponents); the location/weather analysis depends only on venue and date, so this does not affect the findings.
Kansas City / Arrowhead Stadium has no cached real photo; it is represented in the map by a placeholder, never a fabricated image.
